newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan large oil firms' earnings more than halved.
newsitem.headline: Japan large oil firms' earnings more than halved.

text.p: Japan's ten large oil companies reported current profits totalling 40 billion yen in the business year that ended on March 31, down 53.3 percent from a year earlier, an oil industry association said on Friday.
Mitsubishi Oil Co Ltd was the only firm among the ten to suffer a current loss, according to the Petroleum Association of Japan (PAJ).
Mitsubishi Oil's current loss, its first in 12 years, totalled 8.3 billion yen, down sharply from a current profit of 20.7 billion yen the previous year.
Current profit is pre-tax and includes gains and losses from non-operating activities.
Mitsubishi Oil said the decline could mainly be attributed to financial support it provided to affiliated gasoline stations caught in a vicious price war.
The other nine companies reported a year-on-year decline in current profits.
Japan's oil industry faces an uphill battle to improve earnings a year after industry deregulation, which deprived firms of their virtually exclusive right to import oil products.
Faced with competition from overseas, refiners were forced to bring down their wholesale prices at a time when global crude oil prices were rising.
In February, Mitsubishi Oil and Showa Shell Sekiyu KK said they were thinking of merging their distribution and refining divisions in a bid to slash costs.

The PAJ's study took its figures from the earnings performance of the following ten companies, all of which close their business year on March 31: Idemitsu Kosan Co Ltd, Nippon Oil Co Ltd, Toa Oil Co Ltd, Koa Oil Co Ltd, Cosmo Oil Co Ltd, Kygnus Sekiyu KK, Kyushu Oil Co Ltd, Mitsubishi Oil Co Ltd, Japan Energy Corp and General Sekiyu KK.
Although the majority of Japanese oil companies close their books in March, some major firms with to overseas oil firms, including Showa Shell Sekiyu KK operate on a January-December business year.
